source.title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)

accepted.question_text: Let J_Λ^(α) denote the integral form of the Jack superpolynomial indexed by a superpartition Λ, defined by J_Λ^(α)=v_Λ(α)P_Λ^(α), and let its monomial expansion be J_Λ^(α)=Σ_{Ω≤Λ} v_{ΛΩ}(α) m_Ω. Is it true that for every pair of superpartitions Ω≤Λ, each expansion coefficient v_{ΛΩ}(α) is a polynomial in α with integer coefficients, i.e. v_{ΛΩ}(α)∈ℤ[α]?
accepted.context_brief: Integrality of integral-form Jack superpolynomial coefficients

evidence.quote: We define the integral form of the Jack superpolynomials, to be denoted J^(α)_Λ, as (3.38) J^(α)_Λ = v_Λ(α)P^(α)_Λ,
When expanded in the monomial basis, i.e. (3.39) J^(α)_Λ = ∑_{Ω≤Λ} v_{ΛΩ}(α) m_Ω, where v_{ΛΛ}(α) = v_Λ(α), we have the following conjecture.
Conjecture 3.1 – [14] The coefficients v_{ΛΩ}(α) are polynomials in α with integer coefficients, that is, they belong to Z[α].

accepted.question_text: Find a combinatorial description for the coefficients v_{ΛΩ}(α) in the monomial expansion J_Λ^(α)=Σ_{Ω≤Λ} v_{ΛΩ}(α)m_Ω of the integral-form Jack superpolynomials, analogous to the known combinatorial description in the ordinary Jack-polynomial case cited as [31].
accepted.context_brief: Combinatorial formula for Jack superpolynomial integral-form coefficients

evidence.quote: We define the integral form of the Jack superpolynomials, to be denoted J^(α)_Λ, as (3.38) J^(α)_Λ = v_Λ(α)P^(α)_Λ,
When expanded in the monomial basis, i.e. (3.39) J^(α)_Λ = ∑_{Ω≤Λ} v_{ΛΩ}(α) m_Ω,
Open problem 3.2 – Find a combinatorial description, analogous to that of [31], for the expansion coefficients v_{ΛΩ}(α) in (3.39).

accepted.question_text: Fix k≥1 and N≥k+1, and let F_N^(k) be the ideal of symmetric superpolynomials in N even variables x_1,…,x_N and N odd variables θ_1,…,θ_N over ℂ that vanish whenever x_1=x_2=⋯=x_{k+1}. For α_{k,2}=-(k+1), do the Jack superpolynomials P_Λ^(α_{k,2}) indexed by all (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions Λ form a basis of F_N^(k)?
accepted.context_brief: Basis conjecture for admissible Jack superpolynomials

evidence.quote: Throughout this section, we set (3.47) α_{k,r} = -(k + 1)/(r - 1)
A superpartition Λ with exactly N parts is (k,r,N)-admissible if it satifies [32] (3.48) Λ^⊛_i − Λ^*_i+k ≥ r for all 1 ≤ i ≤ N − k

Let F^(k)_N denote the ideal of symmetric superpolynomials (over C) in N (even) variables x = x1, . . . , xN and in N (odd) variables θ = θ1, . . . , θN that satisfy (3.49) f(x, θ) = 0 whenever x1 = x2 = . . . = xk+1.
Conjecture 3.3 – The Jack superpolynomials P^(α_{k,2})_Λ(x1, . . . , xN, θ1, . . . , θN), with Λ (k, 2, N)-admissible, form a basis of the space F^(k)_N.

accepted.question_text: Determine the connection between admissible superpartitions and superconformal field theory: specifically, explain how the basis of states for the irreducible Neveu–Schwarz modules in the minimal superconformal model M(2,4p) is related to admissible superpartitions and the corresponding admissible Jack superpolynomials.
accepted.context_brief: Admissible superpartitions and superconformal field theory

evidence.quote: Therefore, the ideal I^(k,r)_N defines a module over a subalgebra of the centerless Neveu-Schwarz algebra (i.e. the super-Virasoro algebra)

Open problem 3.4 – Connection with superconformal field theory. The basis of states for the irreducible Neveu-Schwarz modules in minimal superconformal model M(2, 4p) can be characterized by admissible superpartitions [34].

accepted.question_text: Let ρ̂_{q,t} be the automorphism of the supersymmetric function ring defined on power sums by ρ̂_{q,t}(p_r)=(-1)^{r-1}(1-q^r)/(1-t^r)·p_r and ρ̂_{q,t}(~p_r)=Σ_{Λ⊢(r|1)} z_Λ^{-1} ω_Λ ∏_i(1-q^{Λ^s_i}) p_Λ. For every superpartition Λ, does this automorphism satisfy the second duality relation ρ̂_{q,t}(P_Λ(q,t)) = t^{|Λ'^a|} Q_{Λ'}(t,q)?
accepted.context_brief: Second duality conjecture for Macdonald superpolynomials

evidence.quote: There is a second duality relation which is defined as follow. Let ρ̂_{q,t} be the automorphism determined by (4.56) ρ̂_{q,t}(p_r) = (−1)^{r−1}(1 − q^r)/(1 − t^r) p_r, ρ̂_{q,t}(~p_r) = ∑_{Λ⊢(r|1)} z^{-1}_Λ ω_Λ ∏_i (1 − q^{Λ^s_i}) p_Λ
Conjecture 4.1 – From the action of ρ̂_{q,t}, we have the (second) duality relation (4.57) ρ̂_{q,t}(P_Λ(q, t)) = t^{|Λ'^a|}Q_{Λ'}(t, q).

accepted.question_text: For superpartitions Λ and Ω of the same degree, define the specialization u_Λ by x_{w_Λ(i)}=q^{-Λ^*_i}t^{i-1}, and define the normalized Macdonald superpolynomial ~P_Λ = P_Λ / P_Λ(u_{(δ^m;)}). Is the symmetry relation ~P_Λ(u_Ω)=~P_Ω(u_Λ) always true?
accepted.context_brief: Evaluation symmetry for normalized Macdonald superpolynomials

evidence.quote: The specialization u_Λ gives the variables x1, . . . , xN the values (4.65) u_Λ : x_{w_Λ(i)} = q^{−Λ^*_i} t^{i−1}, i = 1, 2, . . . , N,
We now define the following normalized version of P_Λ as (4.68) ~P_Λ = P_Λ/P_Λ(u_{(δ^m;)}), which is such that ~P_Λ(ǫ_{q,t}) = 1.
Conjecture 4.2 – (Symmetry). [41] For any superpartitions Λ, Ω of the same degree, we have (4.69) ~P_Λ(u_Ω) = ~P_Ω(u_Λ).

accepted.question_text: Let J_Λ(q,t)=h_Λ^{lo}(q,t)P_Λ(q,t) be the integral form of the Macdonald superpolynomial, let φ_t be the automorphism defined by φ_t(p_r)=(1-t^r)^{-1}p_r and φ_t(~p_s)=~p_s, and let H_Λ(q,t)=φ_t(J_Λ(q,t)). When H_Λ(q,t) is expanded in the Schur-superpolynomial basis as H_Λ(q,t)=Σ_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q,t)s_Ω, are all coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients?

evidence.quote: The integral form associated to the super-Macdonald P_Λ(q, t) is given by (4.70) J_Λ(q, t) = h^{lo}_Λ(q, t)P_Λ(q, t).

Let φ_t be the automorphism of A determined by (4.71) φ_t(p_r) = (1 − t^r)^{−1} p_r, (r ≥ 1); φ_t(~p_s) = ~p_s, (s ≥ 0), and then define the modified Macdonald superpolynomial H_Λ(q, t) as (4.72) H_Λ(q, t) = φ_t(J_Λ(q, t)).
The expansion of H_Λ(q, t) in the Schur superpolynomial basis s_Ω (see (4.15)) defines the (q, t)-Kostka coefficients, (4.73) H_Λ(q, t) = ∑_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q, t) s_Ω
Conjecture 4.3 – (Positivity). [23] The coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q, t) are, for all superpartitions Λ and Ω, polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients, that is, they belong to N[q, t].

accepted.question_text: Obtain Littlewood–Richardson rules for the superspace structure constants c^Γ_{ΛΩ} and c̄^Γ_{ΛΩ} defined by the products s_Γ s_Ω = Σ_Λ c^Λ_{ΓΩ} s_Λ and s̄_Γ s̄_Ω = Σ_Λ c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} s̄_Λ, equivalently describing the generalized Littlewood–Richardson coefficients that govern skew Schur functions in superspace.

evidence.quote: Define c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} and c^Λ_{ΓΩ} to be respectively such that (6.26) s̄_Γ s̄_Ω = ∑_Λ c̄^Λ_{ΓΩ} s̄_Λ and s_Γ s_Ω = ∑_Λ c^Λ_{ΓΩ} s_Λ.
Proposition 6.6 – We have (6.27) s_{Λ/Ω} = ∑_Γ c̄^{Λ'}_{Γ'Ω'} s_Γ and s̄_{Λ/Ω} = ∑_Γ c^Λ_{ΩΓ} s̄_Γ.
Open problem 6.7 – An interesting problem would be to obtain Littlewood-Richardson rules for the coefficients c^Γ_{ΛΩ}, c̄^Γ_{ΛΩ}.

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the arXiv PDF 1903.07777 and mapped the document structure. Open-problem material is concentrated in Sections 3.5, 3.6, 4.6, and 6.4.
Converted Conjecture 3.1 into a self-contained coefficient-integrality question by inlining the definition of the integral form and its monomial expansion.
Rewrote Open problem 3.2 to state explicitly which coefficients require a combinatorial description.
Expanded Conjecture 3.3 by inlining the admissibility condition, the parameter α_{k,2}, and the definition of F_N^(k).
Kept Open problem 3.4 as a connection problem, making the Neveu-Schwarz and minimal-model context explicit.
Expanded Conjecture 4.1 into a standalone duality question using the source-defined automorphism ρ̂_{q,t}.
Expanded Conjecture 4.2 by including the specialization u_Λ and the normalized polynomial ~P_Λ.
Expanded Conjecture 4.3 into a standalone positivity question by defining J_Λ(q,t), φ_t, H_Λ(q,t), and the coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q,t).
Rewrote Open problem 6.7 as a self-contained request for Littlewood-Richardson rules, using the product definitions of the superspace coefficients.
